paper_metadata.title: Neural oscillations track recovery of consciousness in acute traumatic brain injury patients

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study clearly defines the target population (moderate-to-severe TBI in ICU), recruitment setting (UCLA Neuroscience/Trauma ICU), and explicit inclusion/exclusion criteria based on GCS and CT evidence. While it is a convenience sample from a single center, the clinical characteristics are well-described.

items.label: Source of target population
items.prompt: The source population or population of interest is adequately described for key characteristics (LIST).
items.evidence_snippet: 41 patients admitted at the Ronald Reagan UCLA Medical Center Neuroscience/Trauma ICU from December 2015 to February 2020 following moderate-to-severe TBI.
items.reasoning: The authors specify the clinical setting, timeframe, and the specific condition (TBI severity).

items.prompt: The sampling frame and recruitment are adequately described, including methods to identify the sample sufficient to limit potential bias (number and type used, e.g., referral patterns in health care)
items.evidence_snippet: The sample size was determined by patient availability and was not set a priori.
items.reasoning: Recruitment was based on consecutive availability in a specialized ICU setting, which is standard for acute TBI prognosis studies.

items.label: Recruitment period
items.prompt: Period of recruitment is adequately described
items.evidence_snippet: from December 2015 to February 2020
items.reasoning: The specific dates for the recruitment window are provided.

items.label: Place of recruitment

items.label: Inclusion and exclusion criteria
items.prompt: Inclusion and exclusion criteria are adequately described (e.g., including explicit diagnostic criteria or “zero time” description).
items.evidence_snippet: inclusion criteria were as follows: patients were retained if they demonstrated an admission Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS; Teasdale & Jennett, 1974) score ≤8 or an admission GCS score of 9–14 with computed tomography (CT) evidence of intracranial bleeding.
items.reasoning: Criteria are based on validated clinical scales (GCS) and objective imaging (CT).

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: While the acute analysis has low attrition, the chronic outcome (GOSe) is missing for several patients (approx 10%). The reasons for missingness are partially explained (e.g., death), but a systematic comparison between those with and without 6-month follow-up is missing.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The prognostic factor (EEG ABCD model) is measured using an automated, objective algorithm described in detail. This eliminates the subjectivity of manual scoring and ensures consistency across the sample.

items.label: Definition of the PF
items.prompt: A clear definition or description of 'PF' is provided (e.g., including dose, level, duration of exposure, and clear specification of the method of measurement).
items.evidence_snippet: EEG types, labeled A–D (hence, ABCD model) are summarized in Table 1... automated methods based on quantitative EEG criteria.
items.reasoning: The ABCD types are defined by specific spectral peak combinations (Theta, Alpha, Beta).

items.label: Valid and Reliable Measurement of PF
items.prompt: Method of PF measurement is adequately valid and reliable to limit misclassification bias (e.g., may include relevant outside sources of information on measurement properties, also characteristics, such as blind measurement and limited reliance on recall).
items.evidence_snippet: we spline-interpolated channel-level power spectral densities (PSDs)... identified local maxima... determined the ABCD type using criteria in Table 1.
items.reasoning: The use of an automated algorithm (MATLAB findpeaks) ensures high reliability and removes observer bias.

items.prompt: Continuous variables are reported or appropriate cut-points (i.e., not data-dependent) are used.
items.evidence_snippet: EEG frequency bands were defined as follows... delta, 1–4 Hz; theta, 4–8 Hz; alpha, 8–12 Hz; beta, 12–35 Hz.
items.reasoning: Standard clinical frequency band definitions were used.

items.label: Method and Setting of PF Measurement
items.prompt: The method and setting of measurement of PF is the same for all study participants.
items.evidence_snippet: clinical EEG was recorded continuously for multiple days using a sparse montage with 13–17 channels (Cz reference).
items.reasoning: The recording protocol was standardized across the ICU cohort.

items.label: Proportion of data on PF available for analysis
items.prompt: Adequate proportion of the study sample has complete data for PF variable.
items.evidence_snippet: 10.6% could not be classified according to the ABCD model due to peak combinations that did not fit any ABCD type
items.reasoning: While most data were usable, a significant minority (10.6%) of observations were unclassifiable by the primary model.

items.label: Method used for missing data
items.prompt: Appropriate methods of imputation are used for missing 'PF' data.
items.evidence_snippet: Instances of unclassifiable ABCD type were treated as missing data.
items.reasoning: No imputation was performed; unclassifiable data were simply excluded from the LMMs.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: Outcomes were measured using the GCS and GOSe, which are the gold standards in TBI research. While GOSe was sometimes collected via phone, this is a validated method for this scale.

items.label: Definition of the Outcome
items.prompt: A clear definition of outcome is provided, including duration of follow-up and level and extent of the outcome construct.
items.evidence_snippet: Glasgow Outcome Scale Extended (GOSe... administered approximately 6 months (190 ± 33 days, mean ± SD) postinjury
items.reasoning: The outcome and the timing of assessment are clearly defined.

items.label: Valid and Reliable Measurement of Outcome
items.prompt: The method of outcome measurement used is adequately valid and reliable to limit misclassification bias (e.g., may include relevant outside sources of information on measurement properties, also characteristics, such as blind measurement and confirmation of outcome with valid and reliable test).
items.evidence_snippet: behavioral assessments were performed several times daily using the GCS... GOSe... administered... in-person or by phone
items.reasoning: GCS and GOSe are validated, standard instruments for TBI outcome assessment.

items.label: Method and Setting of Outcome Measurement
items.prompt: The method and setting of outcome measurement is the same for all study participants.
items.evidence_snippet: GCS scores were selected corresponding to the day/time of each patient's randomly resampled EEG observation.
items.reasoning: The temporal linking of EEG and GCS was consistent for all participants.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study performed sophisticated adjustment for confounders, including age, sex, and most importantly, a PCA-based reduction of complex ICU medication data (sedatives/analgesics), which is a major strength in this setting.

items.label: Important Confounders Measured
items.prompt: All important confounders, including treatments (key variables in conceptual model: LIST), are measured.
items.evidence_snippet: categorized medications... into one of five classes: propofol, opioids, benzodiazepines, barbiturates, and dissociatives... AGE... SEX
items.reasoning: Key demographic and treatment-related confounders (sedation) were captured.

items.label: Definition of the confounding factor
items.prompt: Clear definitions of the important confounders measured are provided (e.g., including dose, level, and duration of exposures).
items.evidence_snippet: categorized medications from each EEG observation into one of five classes
items.reasoning: Medications were treated as binary (present/absent) during the observation, rather than precise dosages.

items.label: Valid and Reliable Measurement of Confounders
items.prompt: Measurement of all important confounders is adequately valid and reliable (e.g., may include relevant outside sources of information on measurement properties, also characteristics, such as blind measurement and limited reliance on recall).
items.evidence_snippet: logistic PCA to the resultant matrix of observations medication classes
items.reasoning: The use of logistic PCA is a robust way to handle binary medication data in a statistical model.

items.label: Method and Setting of Confounding Measurement
items.prompt: The method and setting of confounding measurement are the same for all study participants.
items.evidence_snippet: Patients in our study were administered a very large number of medications in the ICU. To appropriately account for medications, we first categorized medications from each EEG observation
items.reasoning: The medication tracking was standardized across the cohort.

items.prompt: Important potential confounders are accounted for in the study design (e.g., matching for key variables, stratification, or initial assembly of comparable groups).

items.prompt: Important potential confounders are accounted for in the analysis (i.e., appropriate adjustment).
items.evidence_snippet: GCS ~ 1 + EEG + AGE + SEX + PC1 + PC2 + (1|PATIENT)
items.reasoning: Multivariable Linear Mixed Models were used to adjust for age, sex, and medication PCs.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The statistical approach was rigorous, using Linear Mixed Models to account for the longitudinal nature of the data and resampling to handle the unbalanced design for chronic outcomes. Multiple testing corrections were applied.

items.label: Presentation of analytical strategy
items.prompt: There is sufficient presentation of data to assess the adequacy of the analysis.
items.evidence_snippet: we used linear mixed models (LMMs) with random intercepts... formula GCS ~ 1 + EEG + AGE + SEX + PC1 + PC2 + (1|PATIENT)
items.reasoning: The model formulas and software used are explicitly stated.

items.label: Model development strategy
items.prompt: The strategy for model building (i.e., inclusion of variables in the statistical model) is appropriate and is based on a conceptual framework or model.
items.evidence_snippet: Our study tested four hypotheses... based on the mesocircuit model
items.reasoning: The analysis was hypothesis-driven based on the established Schiff mesocircuit theory.

items.prompt: The selected statistical model is adequate for the design of the study.
items.evidence_snippet: LMMs with random intercepts... resampling approach that randomly sampled one EEG observation per patient with replacement
items.reasoning: The authors correctly identified that LMMs are needed for repeated measures and resampling is needed for the static GOSe outcome.

items.label: Reporting of results
items.prompt: There is no selective reporting of results.
items.evidence_snippet: we corrected for the four hypothesis tests... using a Bonferroni correction
items.reasoning: The authors reported both significant and non-significant results (e.g., GOSe) and applied strict alpha corrections.
